conventions.convention: The physical brackets are [U]_D = −I_D(U)/4 and [Y]_F = I_F(Y)/2. Raw integrals extract the ordered θ¹θ²barθ¹barθ² and θ¹θ² coefficients. Hermitian conjugation is added once, only to the extracted F action.
Physical chiral components use Φ = a + √2 θψ + 2θ¹θ²𝓕 in chiral coordinates y = x + iθσbarθ; thus ψ_raw = √2ψ and F_raw = 2𝓕.
Spacetime is Minkowski R^(1,3), with metric diag(−1,1,1,1) and natural units ℏ = c = 1. The Wess–Zumino component maps are smooth and coefficientwise compactly supported.
The Kähler patch U is open in C^n and contains zero; K is smooth and real, and g_(i bar j) = ∂ᵢ∂_(bar j)K is positive-definite Hermitian everywhere on U.

Off-shell fields have full even scalar and auxiliary coefficients in a finite exterior algebra. Positivity is asserted only after restricting to the ordinary complex bosonic sector; that sector is not claimed to be preserved by supersymmetry. The conjugation-preserving left-parameter convention is barε = −ε*.
Gauge generators are T_a = −iσ_a/2 and t_a = iT_a = σ_a/2; κ = −2Tr₂. The connection is A_μ = −igB_μ, so D_μ = ∂_μ − igB_μ^a t_(a,R).
Represented matrix curvature and abstract connection-normalized curvature are distinct: ρ_*(𝓦_α) = 𝒞_(α,R)/(2i). Consequently κ_C(𝓦^α,𝓦_α) = Tr₂(𝒞^α𝒞_α)/2 in the fundamental representation.
Supersymmetry acts on the full vector prepotential. Wess–Zumino gauge is a component representative and need not be preserved by an uncompensated variation.

load_bearing.statement: Define the physical action brackets by [U]_D := −I_D(U)/4 and [Y]_F := I_F(Y)/2, with physical chiral expansion Φ(y,θ) = φ(y) + √2 θ^αψ_α(y) + 2θ¹θ²F(y).

Adopt the classical rigid N=1 action S_WZ = ∫d⁴x{[K(barΦ,Φ)]_D + [W(Φ)]_F + h.c.}, with conjugation only on the F action, the specified positive Kähler patch, holomorphic W, finite nilpotent Taylor evaluation, and smooth coefficientwise compactly supported full formal components. Its ordinary complex bosonic auxiliary Lagrangian is g_(i bar j)FⁱbarF^(bar j) + FⁱWᵢ + barF^(bar j)barW_(bar j).

A vector prepotential is a dimensionless smooth even real matrix-valued superfield with the specified chiral supergauge transformations. Its represented curvature is 𝒞_(α,R) = −(1/4)barD^(dotβ)barD_(dotβ)(e^(−2gV_R)D_αe^(2gV_R)), and ρ_(R*)(𝓦_α) = 𝒞_(α,R)/(2i).

In the ordinary complex bosonic zero-derivative sector of the adopted positive-Kähler-metric model, the algebraic field equation is Fⁱ = −g^(i bar j)barW_(bar j), and eliminating F gives V_F = g^(i bar j)WᵢbarW_(bar j) ≥ 0. For the canonical metric this is Σᵢ|Wᵢ|².

Adopt the rigid classical SU(2) action with matter D integrands barΦᵃe^(2gV_Ra)Φᵃ and chiral F integrand κ_C(𝓦^α,𝓦_α)/(4g²) + W_G(Φ), plus its Hermitian conjugate, for the specified finite unitary matter representations, invariant holomorphic superpotential, full formal coefficient fields, and boundary conditions.

concerns.concern: Definition, line 55, simultaneously requires flat chirality barD𝒞 = 0 and the ordinary principal-bundle transition 𝒞_j = Ad_(g_ij(x)^−1)𝒞_i. For a spacetime-dependent transition, differentiating this formula produces a generally nonzero term involving barDg_ij = −iθσ^μ∂_μg_ij; ordinary adjoint patching therefore does not preserve the stated flat chiral constraint. For example, a varying exp(f(x)T₃) transition acting on a noncommuting T₁-valued chiral curvature produces this obstruction. No chiral superspace lift of the transitions is specified. The same missing construction affects post-qftx-n1-gauge-matter-model's assertion that its local superspace densities patch and the global interpretation of pthm-qftx-n1-gauge-matter-off-shell-invariance; the local total-derivative argument itself remains valid. The source transformation uses chiral parameters, rather than arbitrary unlifted g(x): [Martin, §4.9, equations (4.9.4)–(4.9.13)](https://arxiv.org/html/hep-ph/9709356v7#S4.SS9).

The Definition displays '[U]_D = [P_phys U]_F' under compact support, although both brackets were defined as pointwise coefficient extractions. This is generally an equality only after spacetime integration, or modulo a spacetime divergence. Take U = f(x), with f a smooth compactly supported scalar function independent of all odd coordinates. Then [U]_D = 0, whereas the stated derivative conventions give P_raw f = −θ¹θ²□f and [P_phys f]_F = □f/4, which need not vanish pointwise. The following prose acknowledges total derivatives but does not qualify the displayed equality as an integrated identity.

Fact F3 attributes 'the scalar kinetic term in the matter D-term is −(D_μφ)†D^μφ' to post-qftx-n1-gauge-matter-model. That supplier states the superspace action and connection convention but does not display or derive this component term. The example correctly proves covariance of the displayed derivative and density; identifying that density with the action's scalar kinetic term still requires a short component extraction, including its total-divergence qualification, rather than the present exact-supplier attribution.

seams_checked.note: This is reading-order context. The assigned superspace proofs do not invoke the physical BPS definitions or massive-fiber conclusions as premises.
The selected SU(2) group, right-principal connection law, anti-Hermitian generators, κ normalization, positive coupling, metric, and classical scope are retained.

The ordered Grassmann algebra, involution, left derivatives, shifted chiral coordinates, supercharges, and chirality identities are used at their stated smooth finite-coefficient scope. The physical bracket conversion is declared separately.

The ordinary connection and associated-bundle formulas are copied faithfully, but their extension to flat-chiral superfields is unsupported: ordinary x-dependent principal transitions do not preserve flat chirality without specified superspace lifts. See the vector-superfield concern.
The fundamental example uses the ordinary associated-bundle convention φ_j = R(g_ij^−1)φ_i and D = d + ρ_*(A). Its transition calculation agrees with the opened covariant-derivative supplier.
The right-connection transition, SU(2) generators, and A = −igB convention give the displayed two-component covariant derivative with the stated signs.

The N=2 and N=4 postulates preserve the physical bracket factors and represented-versus-abstract curvature dictionary. Extended supersymmetry is explicitly adopted rather than claimed to follow from the N=1 invariance theorem.
The hypermultiplet bilinear example uses the supplied chiral supergauge action and checks invariant pairings algebraically, without claiming extended supersymmetry.

The Wilsonian definition supplies an explicit fixed-real-coupling bridge V = −2gV_30, identifies its curvature with the represented matrix curvature, and retains ρ_*(𝓦_30) = W/(2i). It does not infer quantum measure equivalence from the classical conversion.

The independent pure N=2 ultraviolet datum preserves the brackets and curvature dictionary, distinguishes the adjoint vector chiral field from matter hypermultiplets, and adopts its extended invariance separately.

The O’Raifeartaigh theorem uses only the canonical ordinary-complex F-term potential and auxiliary equation. It explicitly limits minimization to pointwise values and does not treat nonzero constant configurations as compactly supported model fields.

The supersymmetric EFT definition preserves the physical bracket factors and chiral component conversion, while keeping regulated matching, truncation, and field-redefinition hypotheses separate from classical normalization.
